# fethr

> fethr is a featherweight code editor with a first-class AI agent panel. Alpha;
> latest release v0.9.3-alpha (2026-08-22). The name is pronounced "feather".

## What it is

- A minimal, fast code editor where an AI coding agent is a first-class peer
  process, not a bolted-on extension: the editor forwards context (current file,
  selection, attached files, the real git branch) and renders results (streamed
  replies, diff proposals); the intelligence lives in the agent runtime.
- Designed around the front-end/runtime split popularized by Claude Code.
  fethr is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
- No extension platform by design.

## How to run it

- `npx @evojewel/fethr@alpha .` starts a local server bound to 127.0.0.1 and opens
  the OS browser as the shell. `fethr --app` opens a chromeless Chrome/Edge window.
- Native macOS app (Apple Silicon, ~40 MB disk image) attached to each GitHub
  release. It bundles the same Node server as a sidecar, so it needs a system Node
  install (Homebrew or nvm are found automatically) and Claude Code installed.
  Signed but not notarized: macOS blocks the first launch until allowed under
  System Settings > Privacy & Security.
- Both paths need Node 18+ and an existing Claude Code login; there is no API key
  to configure.

## The editor

CodeMirror 6 core (about 660 KB of editor code), file tree with collapsible
folders, syntax highlighting for JS/TS, Python, Markdown, HTML, CSS and JSON, edit
and save (Cmd-S; optional auto-save for typed edits). No Electron. File access is
confined to the launch directory, with symlinks resolved and re-checked. Panels
resize by dragging and persist their widths; Cmd-B collapses the sidebar. A "view" button in the footer picks one of five themes (auto, moss, paper, slate, dawn). The
sidebar header shows the real git branch, read server-side.

## The agent panel

Cmd-J opens it. Runs on the Claude Agent SDK using the machine's Claude Code login.

- Read-only by construction: Read/Grep/Glob inside the workspace only; every
  mutating tool is disabled server-side.
- The sole change mechanism is a propose_edit tool. Proposals render as diff cards
  the writer accepts or rejects; accepted edits apply in the editor buffer
  (undoable with Cmd-Z). Agent-driven changes never trigger auto-save; the writer
  saves. The agent process never writes to disk.
- Live status (thinking / tool / writing), streamed thinking in a collapsible
  block, per-tool activity detail, a stop button, markdown replies.
- Model picker: default, opus, sonnet, haiku, fable 5 (fable folds back to default
  if the account can't reach it). Switching models starts a new conversation.
- Auto mode applies proposals straight to the buffer without a manual Accept;
  off by default. Proposals restored from an earlier session always require a
  manual Accept.
- Context is visible: a pill row above the composer shows the current file, the
  live selection and any files attached via @-mention (autocomplete against the
  workspace). The current git branch is sent as explicit context.
- file:line references in replies (e.g. app.js:42) are clickable and jump the
  editor there.
- Voice input via the browser's Web Speech API (verified in Chromium).
- Chat history persists per project in .fethr/chat.json inside the workspace.

## Privacy

The editor makes one network call on its own: once a day it fetches
https://fethr.dev/version.json (a public file, nothing sent) to learn whether a newer
version exists; a footer checkbox turns it off. The agent panel sends the current file,
the selection and anything attached to Anthropic's API through the user's Claude
Code login, the same as using Claude Code directly.

## Weight, honestly

The editor bundle is about 660 KB. The native app is about 40 MB because it skips
the Agent SDK's bundled copy of the claude binary and uses the system install. The
npx path cannot do the same (npm gives a package no supported way to make a
downstream install skip its own optionalDependencies), so the first `npx` run also
downloads that bundled binary, a few hundred MB, cached by npx afterwards.
